title: Packing list for a week away: personal and shared
dek: Build a one-week packing list around weather, laundry and activities, then assign shared items so essentials do not disappear between bags.
metaDescription: Build a one-week packing list around weather, laundry and activities, then assign shared items so essentials do not disappear between bags.

paragraphs: For a week away, pack documents, payment options, required medicines and aids, phone power, daily toiletries and clothes matched to the forecast and laundry plan. Separate personal items from shared items and name the person packing each shared essential. Clothing counts are a starting estimate, not a rule for every traveler.

The easy items to pack are usually the ones already in sight. The charger still plugged in beside the bed and the medicine needed tomorrow morning are more likely to remain behind. A written list should catch those exceptions, not simply describe a generic suitcase. This guide covers an ordinary week, not expedition equipment or destination-specific medical advice.

body.heading: Example: one adult, mild weather, no laundry
rows: Your needs or activities require spares.
Heat, formal events or limited rewear changes the plan.
Activity or weather requires specialist clothing.
One useful layer plus weather protection as needed
One sleepwear set; worn shoes plus another pair if needed
A specific activity needs different footwear.

body.heading: Treat the example as a decision, not a challenge
paragraphs: Those counts are invented planning choices, not hygiene guidance or a claim that everyone can rewear the same amount. If your week requires uniforms, daily changes, sensory accommodations or bulky equipment, make those needs explicit. A smaller bag is not more important than having what you actually need.

If you rely on laundry, confirm the machine, opening arrangements, cost and drying time. "There is probably a laundry nearby" is not a dependable plan for a late arrival. Without confirmed laundry, do not reduce essential clothing on the assumption that everything can be washed on day three.

body.heading: Pack in an order that catches omissions
items: Write the dates, likely weather, activities and laundry arrangement before selecting clothes. Check the forecast again near departure.
List documents, payment access, medicines, glasses and other essential aids first. Identify what cannot readily be replaced at the destination.
Lay out clothing by its actual use. Count what you wear in transit as part of the total rather than packing an unnecessary extra outfit.
Assign shared items such as an adapter, first-aid supplies or laundry bag to a named person. Keep personal health items with the person who needs them.
Mark items packed only when they are in the bag. Put still-in-use items on a separate morning list with their location.
Check bag limits and item restrictions for the actual transport. Keep essential accessible items in the bag that stays with you.

body.heading: Personal versus shared
rows: Adapter or charger only if actually suitable for everyone
Laundry bag, cleaning items or destination equipment with an owner

body.heading: Flying adds a restriction check
paragraphs: The [TSA travel checklist](https://www.tsa.gov/sites/default/files/tsa-travel-checklist.pdf) states the ordinary US carry-on liquids rule: containers of 3.4 ounces or less, fitting one quart-size bag per passenger. That is about the container and bag, not whether a large bottle is mostly empty. Check exemptions and special items separately with the responsible security authority.

[FAA guidance](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries) requires spare lithium batteries and power banks in the cabin, not checked baggage. Check the device rating and airline restrictions. If your carry-on is taken for gate checking, remove items that cannot be checked before handing it over.

body.heading: What stays accessible
paragraphs: Keep documents, necessary medicines and aids, a usable payment method and critical contact information within reach. A small personal bag can also hold a change of clothes appropriate to your circumstances. Do not assume a replacement is easy because the item is common at home.

For international travel, check destination rules for medicines and other restricted items before packing them. A travel-size container or prescription label does not settle every country's import rules. Ask the appropriate authority or qualified health professional if the requirement is unclear.

body.heading: Finish with the missing-item pass
paragraphs: Check three places: bathroom, charging area and the surface where tomorrow's essentials are waiting. Have each traveler confirm their own personal list where practical. For children or someone needing assistance, make the responsible adult explicit.

Use [the night-before checklist](/guides/night-before-you-travel-checklist) for final timing and home checks rather than reopening every clothing decision. If a required document, medical supply or access arrangement is unresolved, address that first and contact the relevant provider; do not bury it under optional packing improvements.

items.q: How many outfits should I take for seven days?
items.a: Base the number on activities, weather, personal needs and confirmed laundry. Four tops and two bottoms can be a starting example for mild conditions, not a universal minimum. Count what you wear while traveling and add specific clothing only where the trip actually calls for it.

items.q: How do I stop two people packing the same shared item?
items.a: Keep a shared list with one named owner for each item. Confirm suitability, such as the correct plug adapter or enough charging ports, rather than merely ticking charger. Each traveler should still have the personal items they need if bags or people become separated.

items.q: What belongs on the morning packing list?
items.a: Anything still being used: medicines, glasses, phone, charger, daily toiletries and a document taken out for check-in. Write the item and its current location. A short explicit list is more reliable than promising to remember the few things you could not pack last night.
